task.description: REWORK ITERATION 1: CODE-DESIGN-VALIDATOR FAILed the first draft (handoffs/WF02-REQ025-20260817/step-01b-code-design-validator.json) on the 'no implementation code present' check -- Section 6 (6.1 P5/P6, 6.2.2-6.2.6 M2-M6, 6.3) contained near-literal, copy-pasteable Elixir/Ecto code: real with/case/do/else syntax, real Ecto.Multi/Ecto.Query/Ecto.Repo calls (repo.insert/2, from(...) |> repo.one/2, repo.update_all/3), real option keywords (on_conflict:, conflict_target:, prefix:, lock:), real map/struct literals, and append/2's full real implementation body -- not algorithm-shape prose. Rewrite Section 6 entirely in the SAME style as your own req024-event-type-registry.md Section 4.4 (already validator-approved): English-prose conditionals describing what each step does and checks, naming the operation (e.g. 'lock instance_sequence's row FOR UPDATE, or insert it if absent') without writing the actual Ecto/Elixir syntax that performs it. Keep every other section (the design decisions, the error taxonomy, tenant_id derivation via a named reversing function, OQ-1/OQ-5) -- those passed validation and do not need to change; do not re-litigate them, only convert Section 6 from code to prose algorithm steps. Design lib/letflow/design/req025-event-append.md for REQ-025 (Event append). This is Letflow's first multi-table atomic transaction (Ecto.Multi across events/instance_sequence/instance_projections/idempotency-sidecar/event_payload_store) and first requirement needing tenant_id derived from the Ecto :prefix rather than accepted as a caller argument -- both need concrete, unambiguous design, not left to ELIXIR-DEV's judgment. Specify: the exact Ecto.Multi step order and each step's operation; the locking mechanism for instance_sequence (SELECT ... FOR UPDATE-equivalent in Ecto, exact query shape, described in prose not code); the full StoreError-equivalent tagged-tuple/exception error set (one distinct, pattern-matchable case per named failure mode in the requirement text); how tenant_id is derived from :prefix by reversing schema_name_for_tenant/1 (name the reversing function and its signature); the metadata pre-transaction validation (>50 entries, key/value length limits, non-string values) and confirm it runs before the transaction opens, not inside it. Branch feature/WF02-REQ025-20260817 already exists and is checked out.
acceptance_criteria: appending to a terminated instance (status CANCELLED or COMPLETED in instance_projections) returns an error and writes zero rows across all five involved tables, demonstrated by an actual test or iex session against a real Postgres, not just described

two concurrent appends to the same instance_id never receive the same sequence_number -- demonstrated with an actual concurrent test (e.g. Task.async_stream racing two appends) or, if concurrency can't be exercised in this environment, the FOR UPDATE-equivalent locking code path is cited explicitly
appending twice with the same idempotency_key returns is_duplicate: true on the second call and does not insert a second events row, verified against the idempotency sidecar table REQ-023 defines
a payload that fails REQ-024's validate_payload/2 results in zero rows written to events, instance_sequence, or instance_projections -- no partial state
a payload over 4096 bytes is split into events.payload's $ref pointer form plus an event_payload_store row, verified by reading both rows back after append

every row append/1(2) writes (events, instance_sequence, instance_projections, the idempotency sidecar) has tenant_id equal to the tenant whose schema the write targeted, derived internally -- not equal to a caller-supplied tenant_id when the two are deliberately made to disagree in a test, which must fail loudly (not silently attribute to the wrong tenant) rather than succeed
